analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the indexed model and detailed T-041 evidence. GenerationLoopExitThinking.swift:76-129 enables Gemma-only thought exit, validates the close-token round trip, excludes logprobs and defines an 8,192-token answer cap. GenerationLoopGuard.swift:56-103 now retains generated tokens under a locked record, follows split channel markers and requests continuation only for loops inside reasoning. Existing tool-marker disarming remains; GenerationLoopGuardPolicy.swift's patch preserves exclusions for constrained, forced-tool and JSON outputs. No independently supported security regression is established in these changes.
MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift:1444-2151 supplies unchanged surrounding behavior per the complete range map: scoped cache submission, disabled caching for decoded native media, deadline checks, cancellation/terminal draining, output validation and usage forwarding. These are context, not new fixes or regressions. The partial scheduler patch shows pair exclusion and exit-policy plumbing at head 1024-1035, but omits the substantive continuation wiring at 1108-1169.
Integration must examine that wiring, LoopExitThinkingContinuation and bridge pump interactions: enforce the original aggregate output/context budgets (the policy cap alone does not prove enforcement), retain cancellation/deadline and model-pin ownership across rows (T-010, A-018, TB-007), reconcile usage without double billing (A-009), and preserve authenticated cacheScope and donation handling for the resumed prompt (T-041). Check forced close-marker handling against reasoning withholding and tool parsing (A-001), and ensure a continuation cannot survive authorization invalidation (T-053). Token retention at GenerationLoopExitThinking.swift:38-54 adds request-memory cost; its effective bound depends on those omitted budget controls. No changed authentication, encryption, disk storage or privilege control is visible here. Missing continuation evidence is a material coverage limit, not proof of a vulnerability or safety.
